I will still farm the same 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what fits my land, water, and family labor. I have done it for 10 years, so I do not want to change too much at once. I usually start from what I did last year, then adjust a little by price and what I saw in nearby fields. Around here in Quzhou, if wheat fertilizer is too light, tillers are weak and the ears are small. If maize fertilizer is too light, the plants stay thin and the cobs do not fill well. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. Since I have well irrigation, I will use that advantage and make sure wheat gets key water and maize does not suffer badly in dry spells. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid types that local farmers around me already planted with decent results. On 5 mu, I can still manage carefully with family labor, so I do not need to save money by skipping basic inputs. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger, give about 2 irrigations, spray 2 times if disease or aphids show, and use rotary tillage after maize. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen for strong growth, 2 irrigations in key stages if rain is short, 2 pesticide applications, and mostly no-tillage or direct seeding after wheat to save time and catch the season. My target is steady yield, not gambling on very high yield.
